correctness.rationale: First-step degree bound pins the black seed to a vertex and all but one neighbour. Every path-power minimum-degree vertex is an endpoint, and every cycle-power vertex has degree \(2k\); all candidates force after filling an interval. The duplicate count of cyclic intervals with \(L=2k+1\) and \(n\ge L+2\) is precisely one per cyclic \(2k\)-vertex block; other seeds have unique descriptions. Thus \(2k\) and \(n(2k-1)\), and all orbit sizes follow. Independently replayed 83 exhaustive finite cases examining 102073 minimum-cardinality subsets and 96 constructive tests; finite evidence corroborates, not replaces, the proof. The claimed ranges are \(k\ge2\) and \(n\ge k+2\) or \(n\ge2k+3\).

evidence: The complete multipartite theorem and Boyer et al. Proposition 4 cover \(C_{2k+2}^k=K_{2,2,\ldots,2}\), a case excluded by \(n\ge2k+3\).

broader_coverage.reasoning: The generic \(n\ge2k+3\) cycle-power graph is neither complete nor the complete multipartite near-boundary; the new count covers arbitrarily far from the top two polynomial coefficients. For path powers, infinitely many \(n>k+2\) have minimum degree \(k\) far below \(n-2\). Existing general degree-only results do not supply the classification or total number.

originality.rationale: Original contribution is an all-parameter complete classification/count/orbit census of optimal seeds of noncomplete path powers and non-nearly-complete cycle powers. Current primary literature states only minimum values; already known \(k=1\), complete and complete-multipartite boundary cases are credited and excluded. Actual semantic mathematical-record searches did not retrieve an equivalent infinite-family census. A possible undiscovered general neighbourhood-count theorem remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An older general enumeration of minimum zero-forcing sets for circulants or closed-neighborhood interval systems could imply the new formulas without matching the graph-power terminology.
Completeness of the historical literature search cannot be guaranteed; some publisher PDFs could not be inspected in full.
The \(k=1\) and \(n=2k+1\) and \(n=2k+2\) cases, and some \(n-2\) coefficient boundary instances, are known and are explicitly excluded from the originality claim.

value.rationale: Determines the exact number and all structural forms of optimal starting configurations in two infinite families recently motivated by a graph-power zero-forcing paper; cycle-power overlap/collision geometry gives a genuine distinct-orbit decomposition with \(n(2k-1)\) seeds and k natural symmetry types. New information is not implied merely by Z values or finite tests, and the complete natural optimizer classification is a useful refined invariant. The claim excludes known degree-one and dense boundaries and makes no unsupported wider-graph assertion.
